study_options.title: Applied and Engineering Physics
study_options.description: Through coursework and independent study, this coterminal advanced degree program develops your knowledge and skills at the intersection of applied physics and engineering while preparing you for a professional career or doctoral studies.

study_options.title: Anthropology
study_options.description: Enhance your undergraduate degree with a coterminal or terminal master’s degree that prepares you for continued graduate studies or a career in our multicultural and globally-interconnected world. You’ll thrive through advanced coursework, independent specialization, and field research.

study_options.title: Anthropology
study_options.description: Demonstrate your substantial scholarship and the ability to conduct independent research and analysis in anthropology as you prepare for your career in academia or the public or private sectors. By completing advanced coursework and rigorous skills training, you’ll prepare to make original contributions to the discipline of anthropology as well as interpret and present research results.

study_options.title: Applied Physics
study_options.description: Enhance your background in physics or engineering through graduate work in physics. In addition to advanced coursework, you’ll choose an area of specific interest — including accelerator physics, biophysics, condensed matter physics, nanostructured materials, quantum electronics and photonics, quantum optics and quantum information, space science and astrophysics, synchrotron radiation, and applications — and work with faculty members engaged in related fields to conduct research.

study_options.title: Applied Physics
study_options.description: Enhance your background in physics or engineering through graduate work in physics. In addition to advanced coursework, you’ll choose an area of specific interest — including accelerator physics, biophysics, condensed matter physics, nanostructured materials, quantum electronics and photonics, quantum optics and quantum information, space science and astrophysics, synchrotron radiation and applications — and work with faculty members engaged in related fields to conduct research.

study_options.title: Art History
study_options.description: Art History MA is awarded only to doctoral students in Art and Art History as a step toward PhD requirements; the department does not admit standalone MA applicants.

study_options.title: Art Practice
study_options.description: Build upon your strong undergraduate art-practice background or independent studio practice, and further build your portfolio. This master’s degree is offered in painting, sculpture, new genres, and photography.

study_options.title: Art History
study_options.description: This relatively small doctoral program affords you the opportunity to work intensively with faculty in a specialized area you choose as you pursue an advanced degree. Your coursework further enhances your existing background and experience in the general history of art.

study_options.title: Biology
study_options.description: Learn from and work with world-renowned faculty involved in research on ecology, neurobiology, population biology, plant and animal physiology, biochemistry, immunology, cell and developmental biology, genetics, and molecular biology. The program offers you general or specialized study to enhance your current knowledge and experience with graduate-level coursework and advanced research experience.

study_options.title: Biophysics
study_options.description: The Biophysics MS is not a separate or coterm degree program; it may be awarded for a portion of PhD work.

study_options.title: Biophysics
study_options.description: Immerse yourself in two overlapping branches of Biophysics: applying physical and chemical principles and methods to solving biological problems and developing new methods. You’ll train in quantitative approaches to biological problems and perform independent research and analysis in biophysics.

study_options.title: Biology
study_options.description: Learn from and work with world-renowned faculty involved in research on ecology, neurobiology, population biology, plant and animal physiology, biochemistry, immunology, cell and developmental biology, genetics, and molecular biology. You’ll learn how to ask important questions and devise and carry out experiments to answer those questions, make professional presentations, write manuscripts for publication, and become an effective teacher.

study_options.title: Chemistry
study_options.description: Pursue substantial scholarship and independent research and analysis in the field of chemistry that prepare you to make original contributions and to interpret and present the results of such research.

study_options.title: Comparative Literature
study_options.description: Take your linguistic background, breadth of interest in literature, and curiosity about the problems of literary scholarship and theory beyond that of a single national literature through coursework and research in at least three national literatures.

study_options.title: Chemistry
study_options.description: Pursue more profound chemistry knowledge and skills to prepare for a professional career or doctoral studies in fields involving biotechnology, nanotechnology, catalysis, human health, materials, earth and environmental sciences, and more. The Master of Science is available only to current PhD students or as part of a coterminal program.

study_options.title: Classics
study_options.description: Let your coursework and research take you beyond Greek and Roman civilization into the interaction of cultures and societies that influenced the ancient Mediterranean basin with a perspective that crosses geographical, temporal, and thematic territories.

study_options.title: Classics
study_options.description: Continue cultivating your knowledge of Greek and Latin language, literature, philosophy, history, art, and archaeology, and explore specialized fields such as ancient economics, law, papyrology, and science.

study_options.title: Communication
study_options.description: Study how communication techniques and technologies shape who we are, how we govern ourselves, and what kinds of cultures we inhabit. The program offers coterminal and terminal options in tracks, including Media Studies and Journalism.

study_options.title: Economics
study_options.description: The master’s program develops knowledge and skills in economics that you can apply to a professional career or doctoral studies. This program is only open to you in combination with a doctoral degree from Economics or another university department.

study_options.title: Economics
study_options.description: Prepare yourself to make original contributions to the knowledge and application of economics through advanced coursework, rigorous skills training, and independent research and analysis.

study_options.title: English
study_options.description: If you are an advanced undergraduate who wants to take the study of literature to a higher level, then the coterminal MA program is for you. Rigorous graduate-level seminars taught by the department’s renowned faculty and the option of writing an MA thesis offer you an intense intellectual experience.

study_options.title: East Asian Languages and Cultures
study_options.description: Engage with the cultures of China, Japan, Korea, and the greater East Asia region through language, linguistics, literature, film, cultural studies, visual arts, and more.

study_options.title: East Asian Studies
study_options.description: This interdisciplinary program is designed for you if you want to develop a deeper background in the region for a career in nonacademic fields such as business, law, education, journalism, or government service, or you are planning to complete a PhD in the subject area but have not yet decided on your particular focus area.

study_options.title: East Asian Languages and Cultures
study_options.description: Engage with the cultures of China, Japan, Korea, and the greater East Asia region through language, linguistics, literature, film, cultural studies, visual arts, and more.

study_options.title: Education
study_options.description: The Master of Science degrees allow you to specialize in Education Data Science — combining modern data science analyses and computational methods with a deep understanding of learning, schools, and education policy — or Learning, Design, and Technology — integrating powerful contemporary ideas about learning with emergent technologies to design and evaluate learning environments, products, and programs.

study_options.title: Education
study_options.description: Select among options for your Master of Arts in Education including Policy, Organization, and Leadership Studies; Stanford Teacher Education Program; Curriculum and Teacher Education; and individually designed programs.

study_options.title: Education
study_options.description: Become part of the next generation of leading education researchers. You’ll have over 25 areas of specialization or cross-area specialization to choose from. Combined with a research apprenticeship, you’ll be prepared to excel as a university teacher or education researcher.

study_options.title: English
study_options.description: Join our PhD program, where we encourage the production of ambitious, groundbreaking dissertation work across the diverse field interests of our prestigious faculty. Our English department has a tradition of training the next generation of scholars to become leaders in academia and related fields.

study_options.title: Documentary Film and Video
study_options.description: Prepare for a professional film, video, and digital media career and become qualified to teach at the university level. The program is predicated on a paradigm of independent media that values artistic expression, aesthetics, social awareness, and an articulated perspective. You’ll become conversant with the documentary tradition, alternative media, and new directions in documentary.

study_options.title: French
study_options.description: Pursue coursework at the graduate levels in French language, literature, cultural and intellectual history, theory, film, and Francophone studies. The program covers the complex cultural, political, social, scientific, commercial, and intellectual phenomena associated with French-speaking parts of the world, from France and Belgium to Canada, Africa, and the Caribbean.

study_options.title: French
study_options.description: Explore the many facets of French and Francophone cultures from a literary, historical, philosophical, artistic, and more generally interdisciplinary perspective, drawing it into an active dialogue with contemporary global culture. Upon completion, you’ll be capable of teaching French and Francophone literature and culture at all levels, and be able to connect your academic pursuits to real-world problems.

study_options.title: French and Italian
study_options.description: Pursue coursework at all levels in French and Italian language, literature, culture, intellectual history, and more. Course offerings range from small specialized graduate seminars to general courses open to broader audiences.

study_options.title: German Studies
study_options.description: Develop the linguistic and analytic ability to explore the significance of the cultural traditions and political histories of the German-speaking countries of Central Europe. Evaluate the broader and contradictory legacies of the German past, the history of rapid modernization, and the status of Germany, Austria, and Switzerland today.

study_options.title: German Studies
study_options.description: Join our innovative program and vibrant community to prepare yourself to flourish in an academic or non-academic environment. You’ll have direct access to the unique expertise of our faculty to draw on in creating your own courses of study and developing your dissertation project.

study_options.title: History
study_options.description: Further develop your historical knowledge and analytical skills, and better position yourself for a professional career or doctoral studies through advanced coursework, independent work, and specialization leading to a master’s degree.

study_options.title: History
study_options.description: If you’re ready to demonstrate substantial scholarship, our doctoral program prepares you to make original contributions to the knowledge of history through advanced coursework, independent research and analysis, and rigorous skills training. Your faculty advisor will help you tailor your work to your specific areas of interest and support you as you achieve your advanced degree.

study_options.title: Iberian & Latin American Cultures
study_options.description: Build upon your undergraduate foundation through rigorous and highly individualized advanced training in analyzing Iberian, Latin American (including Brazil), and Latinx literature and cultures.

study_options.title: Iberian & Latin American Cultures
study_options.description: Produce innovative, original research and train to be an expert in the cultures of the Iberian Peninsula, Latin America (including Brazil), and Latinx communities in the United States through an emphasis on literary studies and philosophical, historical, and social approaches to cultural issues.

study_options.title: Italian
study_options.description: Pursue coursework at the graduate levels in Italian language, literature, cultural and intellectual history, theory, film, and more. The program covers the complex cultural, political, social, scientific, commercial, and intellectual topics associated with Italian-speaking regions.

study_options.title: Italian
study_options.description: Explore the many facets of Italian cultures from a literary, historical, philosophical, artistic, and more generally interdisciplinary perspective, drawing it into an active dialogue with contemporary global culture. Upon completion, you’ll be capable of teaching Italian literature and culture at all levels, and be able to connect your academic pursuits to real-world problems.

study_options.title: International Policy
study_options.description: Join our interdisciplinary program devoted to rigorous analysis of international policy issues in diplomacy, governance, cyber and international security, global health, and environmental policy. Learn to integrate perspectives from political science, law, economics, history, and other disciplines, conduct original research, and implement solutions addressing global problems.

study_options.title: Latin American Studies
study_options.description: This interdisciplinary program consists of a core set of courses surveying the Latin American region’s history, politics, society, ecology, and culture; advanced language training; and in-depth coursework. You’ll choose a course of study suited to your interests.

study_options.title: Linguistics
study_options.description: Develop your knowledge of linguistics and prepare for a professional career or doctoral study in linguistics or related disciplines.

study_options.title: Linguistics
study_options.description: Through the completion of advanced coursework and strong methodological and analytical training, you’ll prepare to make original contributions to knowledge in linguistics, articulate the results of your work, and demonstrate its significance to linguistics and related fields.

study_options.title: Mathematics
study_options.description: This coterminal degree is intended for undergraduates with a strong background in mathematics. This is evidenced by successfully completing particular courses offered by the Stanford Mathematics Department with a grade of A- or better.

study_options.title: Mathematics
study_options.description: Through a specified course sequence, area examinations, and a dissertation, earn your doctoral degree in Mathematics. You’ll lead and participate in seminars and colloquia in your chosen areas of interest.

study_options.title: Master of Liberal Arts
study_options.description: Our flexible, interdisciplinary program is ideal for returning adult students who seek a broad education in the liberal arts, including art, history, literature, music, philosophy, political science, science, and theology.

study_options.title: Modern Thought and Literature
study_options.description: Learn how the histories and methods of particular disciplines shape knowledge and, most importantly, how interdisciplinary methods reshape objects of study. You’ll produce innovative analyses of diverse texts, forms, and practices in many fields of study.

study_options.title: Modern Thought and Literature
study_options.description: Become a leader in redefining the cutting edge of many interdisciplinary fields and reshape how disciplinary scholarship is understood and practiced in fields such as American studies, ethnic studies, film studies, social and cultural studies, and women's studies, as well as English and comparative literature.

study_options.title: Musical Arts
study_options.description: The Doctor of Musical Arts in composition is offered to students who demonstrate substantial training in the field and high promise of attainment as composers. You’ll achieve breadth through studies in other branches of music and in relevant fields outside of music.

study_options.title: Music
study_options.description: Advance your knowledge on the integration of music perception, music-related signal processing and controllers, synthesis, performance, and composition.

study_options.title: Music
study_options.description: Select among doctoral focus areas and learn to make original contributions to the knowledge and practice of music and to interpret and present the results of such work in appropriate venues and publications.

study_options.title: Political Science
study_options.description: The Master of Arts in Political Science is open to current Stanford University doctoral or professional school students only.

study_options.title: Political Science
study_options.description: Become a Political Science scholar by refining your knowledge in a wide variety of fields in the discipline, including American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, Political Theory, and Political Methodology.

study_options.title: Psychology
study_options.description: Further develop your knowledge and skills in psychology and prepare for a professional career or doctoral studies by completing graduate-level courses and experience with independent work and specialization.

study_options.title: Psychology
study_options.description: Demonstrate substantial scholarship and the ability to conduct independent research and analysis in psychology. You’ll concentrate on one of several areas within the field as you emphasize your development of research competence, skills, and attitudes for a career of continuing research productivity.

study_options.title: Philosophy
study_options.description: Stanford’s PhD program is among the world’s best. You’ll train in traditional core areas of philosophy and have opportunities to explore many subfields, such as the philosophy of literature, nineteenth-century German philosophy, medieval philosophy, and more.

study_options.title: Philosophy
study_options.description: Choose between three Master of Arts programs in Philosophy: a general program, a special program in the philosophy of language, or a special program in symbolic systems.

study_options.title: Public Policy
study_options.description: Develop the advanced skills necessary to assess the performance of alternative approaches to policy making and implementation, evaluate program effectiveness, understand the political constraints faced by policy-makers, and appreciate the conflicts in fundamental human values that often animate policy debate.

study_options.title: Public Policy
study_options.description: This professional degree program provides the academic content of the Master of Arts program with one concentration tailored to your primary degree program or your interests and skills.

study_options.title: Russian, East European and Eurasian Studies
study_options.description: This one-year interdisciplinary program delivers a strong grounding in historical and contemporary change processes in the Russian Federation, East Europe, the Caucasus, and Central Asia.

study_options.title: Religious Studies
study_options.description: Through advanced academic work and research, you’ll specialize in a particular period, topic, or corpus of materials while learning to teach and produce scholarly work.

study_options.title: Religious Studies
study_options.description: This coterminous degree deepens your knowledge of the intellectual, ethical, and sociopolitical issues in the world's religions.

study_options.title: Slavic Languages and Literatures
study_options.description: Deepen your study of Russian language, literature, literary and cultural history, theory, and criticism through graduate-level coursework.

study_options.title: Slavic Languages and Literatures
study_options.description: Become a leader in the field by further broadening your geographic, linguistic, and intellectual range of Slavic culture through formal, historical, and philosophical approaches in literature, history and memory studies, digital techniques, and linguistic anthropology.

study_options.title: Sociology
study_options.description: Available as a coterminal program for undergraduates or as a program for PhD candidates in Sociology or other advanced degree programs, the Master of Arts degree delivers graduate-level coursework that deepens your understanding of the field.

study_options.title: Sociology
study_options.description: Through advanced coursework and ambitious, independent research, you’ll develop methodological skills, substantive knowledge, and mentorship to make significant and impactful contributions to sociological knowledge.

study_options.title: Statistics
study_options.description: Prepare for your research careers in statistics or probability — either applied or theoretical — through advanced coursework and independent research opportunities.

study_options.title: Symbolic Systems
study_options.description: Deepen your understanding of the vocabulary, theoretical background, and technical skills to participate in contemporary interdisciplinary research, specifically into questions about language, information, and intelligence—both human and machine.

study_options.title: Statistics
study_options.description: Available as a coterminal program for undergraduates or as a terminal program for graduates, the Master of Science advances your knowledge of statistics with graduate-level coursework that complements many career paths.

study_options.title: Theater and Performance Studies
study_options.description: Through a program with a rigorous study of critical theory, textual history, elements of production, and embodied research, you’ll prepare yourself to work at the leading edge of both scholarly and performance practice.

study_options.title: Curriculum and Teacher Education
study_options.description: Curriculum and Teacher Education MA: graduate study in curriculum and teacher education; this specialization will not admit in 2027-28.

study_options.title: Global and Comparative Education
study_options.description: Global and Comparative Education MA: education study across global and comparative contexts.

study_options.title: International Education Policy Analysis
study_options.description: International Education Policy Analysis MA: education-policy study with international scope.

study_options.title: Policy, Organization, and Leadership Studies
study_options.description: Policy, Organization, and Leadership Studies MA: preparation for leadership in preK-12 and higher education.

study_options.title: Stanford Teacher Education Program (STEP)
study_options.description: Stanford Teacher Education Program MA: 12-month teacher preparation ending in a preliminary California credential; choose Elementary or one of five Secondary subject fields.

study_options.title: Education MA / MBA joint degree
study_options.description: Joint Education MA/MBA: two-year full-time program combining GSE education coursework and GSB MBA study for educational management.

study_options.title: Education MA / JD joint degree
study_options.description: Joint Education MA/JD: law and education-policy program; students begin at the Law School and combine legal study with individualized GSE work.

study_options.title: Education MA / MPP joint degree
study_options.description: Joint Education MA/MPP: two-year/six-quarter degree; first year combines GSE and public-policy cores and a POLS project, second year centers on MPP practicum and remaining requirements.

study_options.title: Education Data Science
study_options.description: Education Data Science MS: education-focused data-science study; basic programming preparation and a track-specific supplement are required.

study_options.title: Learning Design and Technology
study_options.description: Learning Design and Technology MS: prepares students to design and evaluate research-grounded learning environments, products, and programs using emerging technologies.

facts.value: Applicants must hold, or expect before enrollment to hold, a U.S. bachelor’s degree or international equivalent from a recognized institution. WES evaluation is not required with application; admitted international-degree holders may be asked for WES verification after accepting an offer.
conditions: Credential must be conferred before enrollment.

facts.value: For 2027-28 entry, absent an exemption, official TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic required: minimum consideration TOEFL 90 (before 2026-01-21), TOEFL 4.5 (on/after), or IELTS 7; programs may set higher thresholds. Valid two years; earliest date Sep. 1, 2024.
conditions: Exempt if U.S. citizen/permanent resident, first language English, qualifying degree from university where all instruction was in English, or 2 consecutive years full-time professional/education experience in English within last 10 years.
Self-reported scores permit initial review; official scores may be required for verification.
exceptions: Applicants below TOEFL 109 (pre-Jan. 21) / 5.5 (on/after) or IELTS 8 must take the English Placement Test before first quarter; no exceptions.
facts.canonical_shared_policy_reference: stanford shared graduate admissions policy evidence; retain this scoped alias only

facts.value: Each program separately marks GRE General/Subject required, optional, or not considered. Required scores sent officially; self-reported scores suffice initially. Valid five years; earliest date for 2027-28 entry Sep. 1, 2021.
conditions: Program-specific policy remains to be reconciled from the live directory/department pages.

facts.value: Central application gathers background, academic history/transcripts, applicable tests, experience, three academic/professional references, statement of purpose, program supplement and additional information. Programs may add essays, writing samples, portfolio, audition, CV or other items.
conditions: Department instructions set program-specific materials.

exceptions: A single Biosciences PhD application may name two Home Programs. Concurrent application to one nonprofessional and one or more professional school programs is allowed.

facts.value: 2027-28 application is open. Each program sets its own deadline. Submit materials by that deadline and finalize/pay by 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.

facts.value: USD 125, nonrefundable; pay on submission by credit card or U.S. checking-account bank transfer.

facts.value: Before submitting, applicants may request GRE fee reduction, eligible-program participation, or school-based waiver. Submit at least 10 business days before program deadline for timely decision.
conditions: GRE reduction requires U.S. citizen/permanent resident and ETS voucher.
Participation waiver needs signed proof of good-standing participation.
School criteria and availability vary; Medicine offers school waiver to doctoral applicants only.

facts.value: Graduate study generally requires full-time enrollment (at least 8 units per academic quarter) and significant campus presence, unless the degree program approves reduced/minimal presence.
facts.canonical_shared_policy_reference: stanford shared graduate admissions policy evidence; retain this scoped alias only

facts.value: University minimum for most master’s programs: 45 Stanford units, all 100-level or above, with at least 50% primarily for graduate students (typically 200-level+). Coterminal candidates have three years from first graduate quarter. Program requirements may exceed these minima.
facts.canonical_shared_policy_reference: stanford shared graduate admissions policy evidence; retain this scoped alias only

facts.value: Individually Designed MA in Education is intended for current Stanford doctoral students in a PhD outside GSE. Admission follows GSE consultation and an individualized plan; complete 45 units including at least 27 GSE units within three years, then file Graduate Authorization Petition.
conditions: Not an external entry route.

facts.value: GSE takes a limited number of Stanford undergraduates into MA/MS coterm study after at least 120 units toward graduation; undergraduate department approval and GSE admission both required.

GSE MA specializations include Curriculum and Teacher Education, Global and Comparative Education, International Education Policy Analysis, Policy, Organization and Leadership Studies, plus joint MA/MBA, MA/JD and MA/MPP. MS offerings include Education Data Science and Learning, Design, and Technology. STEP is a 12-month MA with preliminary California credential; GSE also lists Teaching of Physics MA.
conditions: Bulletin award rows group specializations; current admissions route must be checked per track.

facts.value: For 2027-28 entry, GSE PhD deadline is November 16, 2026; MA/MS deadline is January 7, 2027. Knight-Hennessy applicants to GSE must separately meet the November 16, 2026 KHS program deadline.

GRE is not required for 2027-28; applicants may submit optional scores without penalty. Applicants not meeting the central English exemption must meet GSE minimum TOEFL iBT 100 before Jan 21 2026 or 5 after that date, or IELTS Academic 7.5.

Core GSE application asks for 1-2 page single-spaced 12-point statement of purpose, resume/CV, three recommendations, and transcripts from every college/university attended at least one full-time academic year. Upload PDFs/scanned records; current in-progress transcript accepted before degree conferral. Foreign-language transcripts need complete literal translation; admitted students later send official records.

Doctoral program committees may interview. Writing sample is not required for CTE, DAPS, LSTD, or Economics of Education; required 10+ page research-oriented samples for Anthropology of Education, Educational Linguistics, History of Education, Global and Comparative Education, Philosophy of Education; required research samples for EDS, Higher Education, Sociology of Education and RILE. LSTD and RILE applicants under SHIPS must apply to that area and another SHIPS subplan. RILE sample topic must relate to race, inequality and/or language; 1,000-5,000 words preferred. The History/Social Science Education PhD area will not admit for 2027-28.
conditions: Some area committees may interview; others state no interview.

facts.value: DAPS, Economics of Education, Education Data Science, Educational Policy, Higher Education, and Sociology of Education specify supplemental essays/skills questions; respond to each area-specific prompt on the GSE page.

For 2027-28: CTE MA will not admit. EDS MS has no writing sample or interview but requires supplemental essays/skills matrix and basic programming experience/coursework; LDT MS has no writing sample/interview and uses a program-specific statement and short answers. GCE/IEPA MA requires an English research writing sample of at least 10 pages and track-specific statement. POLS MA requires a writing sample up to 10 pages and supplemental essays.
conditions: CTE closure applies to the stated 2027-28 cycle only.

facts.value: STEP applicants choose Elementary or one of five Secondary subject areas (English, history/social science, math, science, world languages). The 12-month full-time program leads to MA plus preliminary California teaching credential. STEP requires a 750-1,250 word essay (max 3 pages), resume, three recommendations, and transcripts for each institution attended at least one year. Current page contains inconsistent 2026-27/2027 cohort term references; follow current application and the 2027-28 MA deadline.
conditions: The historical cycle/start-term mismatch needs live application confirmation.

facts.value: MFA applicants submit an online SlideRoom portfolio by deadline; $10 SlideRoom fee. Include typed work list with date, medium, size, title and viewing instructions. Still-image total max 20; time-based selection max 10 minutes (preferred excerpt 5 minutes). SOP no more than two pages; first sentence must name program and area. Three references, postsecondary transcripts for each full-time institution attended at least one academic year. GRE not required; department states TOEFL for applicants whose first language is not English and IELTS is not accepted, while current central exemptions apply.
conditions: Art & Art History page says TOEFL is required when the applicant’s first language is not English and IELTS is not accepted; central Graduate Admissions lists TOEFL or IELTS and exemptions. Confirm which stricter rule the Art Practice application currently enforces.

facts.value: Autumn-only entry, December 1 at 9 p.m. Pacific deadline; all materials including tests/recommendations/portfolio must arrive by deadline. Department normally provides support package through fellowship plus teaching assistantships, including tuition support, salary and small materials grants; two-year full-time program, typically admits up to five yearly.
conditions: Finalists must travel to Stanford for late-February faculty/student interview. Funding wording is typical/normal rather than guaranteed individual award.

facts.value: Submit one 5-8 page analytical essay on a documentary film/topic as PDF; submit SlideRoom portfolio with film/video work where applicant had creative control if possible. Total sample runtime max 15 minutes, with synopsis, clip runtime and applicant role; minimal production experience may be represented by strongest work in another visual medium. No production-assistant-only work. SlideRoom fee is $6. SOP max two pages; three recommendations and transcripts for institutions attended full-time for at least one year.

Autumn 2027-28 application materials due December 1 at 9 p.m. Pacific; no midyear entry. Two consecutive years in residence. First year fellowship includes stipend and tuition; second-year TA eligibility includes salary and tuition allowance. Production funds also offered.
conditions: Second-year TA support is eligibility, not guaranteed award.

facts.value: Music PhD/DMA applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree; PhD/DMA applicants are expected to have preparation equivalent to a Music bachelor’s. Terminal MA Music, Science, and Technology targets applicants with undergraduate engineering, science, music, arts, or a degree including engineering mathematics. Application requires SOP, three recommendations, unofficial transcripts for each school attended at least one year; MA/PhD also require scholarly writing sample. DMA composition adds complete composition list and links to representative scores and 3-6 audio/video recordings.

GRE is optional for all Music graduate programs. Application for September entry opens late September/early October; completed application due the second Tuesday in December. TOEFL is required for international applicants whose primary language is not English unless they meet waiver requirements. Department does not provide its own fee waiver.
conditions: Program-specific 2027 cycle deadline is in the central directory; department page describes second-Tuesday rule.

facts.value: Doctoral-level Music applicants are expected to have preparation equivalent to a bachelor’s in Music; department suggests comparing prior study to Stanford Music bachelor’s requirements to identify missing theory/history preparation. After admission, incoming doctoral students take dictation and theory diagnostics; musicologists/composers take piano proficiency; ethnomusicologists take piano/other instrument proficiency or non-Western musical traditions test; musicologists take Western-art-music history/repertoire test. Deficiencies may delay TA assignment until remedied.

The terminal History MA is for students who do not intend to continue into Stanford History’s PhD; admitted terminal MA students may not apply to enter the department PhD while working on the MA. Autumn-only entry. Apply through central graduate application with statement of purpose, three recommendations, scanned transcripts for every college attended at least one year, and a 10-25 page history writing sample. GRE general is not required; confirm English testing against central 2027-28 rules. 2027-28 application deadline is December 1, 2026.
conditions: Department page states “11:59 p.m. EST” while central application deadline instructions state 11:59 p.m. Pacific; rely on the live application deadline screen for submission timezone.

facts.value: History MA candidates, terminal and coterminal, receive no departmental funding; any separately awarded university-wide scholarship is not established by this source.

History admits a limited number of Stanford undergraduates to the coterm MA. Applicants specify a field and faculty advisor and need 3.75 GPA in History courses (or equivalent preparation if not a History major). Requirements include coterm application, statement, Stanford transcript, 10-25 page history sample, three recommendations (at least two from History faculty; one from current advisor and one from prospective MA advisor), preliminary program proposal and course-transfer information. Spring-quarter entry only; 2026-27 deadline December 1, 2026. Courses cannot double-count toward both degrees.

scope.cycle: 2026-2027 Spring and 2027-2028 Autumn terms as separately published

conditions: Coterm admissions are an internal undergraduate route and must not be treated as external terminal admission.

facts.value: History guarantees five years of continuous 12-month funding for doctoral students who remain actively enrolled and in good academic standing. Package combines fellowship and assistantship support and provides tuition, stipend/salary, summer stipend and health insurance. Students may separately apply for relocation, conference-travel and research grants.
conditions: Five-year guarantee has active-enrollment and good-standing conditions.

facts.value: EALC applicants need at least three years of training in the language of intended specialization; a prior EALC undergraduate major is not required. Applicants must seek graduate study in a scholarly field (e.g., literature/culture, linguistics, archaeology or Trans-Asian studies), not merely language acquisition.

EALC MA requires a research/writing sample of approximately 15 pages and three recommendations; applicants upload transcripts and the department may contact finalists for Zoom interviews. Students normally complete 45 units and enroll in at least 8 units each quarter. EALC provides limited tuition fellowships to admitted MA students and encourages outside funding.
conditions: Three recommendations, writing sample and transcript requirements apply to the EALC MA route.

facts.value: EALC offers five years of 12-month PhD funding through fellowship, research-assistantship and teaching-assistantship support; students are encouraged to seek outside fellowships.

Comparative Literature PhD: scholarly literary-critical/analytic sample about 5,000 words in English; creative writing is not a substitute. French and Italian graduate programs: two 20-page samples, one in English and one in French or Italian. German Studies: approximately 5,000 words of scholarly analysis in German or English. Iberian and Latin American Cultures: two 20-page samples, one English and one Spanish. Slavic Languages and Literatures: about 20 pages in English analyzing Slavic texts; a short Russian or other relevant-language sample is optional.

Slavic PhD students are required to learn/read Russian, one quarter of Old Church Slavonic, and at least two other languages relevant to research (often French, German or another Slavic language, with alternatives depending on research interests).

Classics PhD application asks for an academic paper in the field, 15-25 pages, and a CV listing language qualifications; ancient-language preparation should be demonstrated by works read in the original and modern-language proficiency may be described by level and years studied. The department says a strong Classics or related-field background is expected.
conditions: Department page’s English-test wording should be reconciled with current university exemption and accepted-test policy.

facts.value: English PhD deadline is December 1, 2026. Submit a critical/scholarly writing sample 12-25 pages (excluding references), preferably in intended area and clear of grading comments. Statement should ideally be 500-600 words and may not exceed 1,000 words.

The 2026-27 Bulletin has a Classics MA degree row, while the Classics Graduate Admissions page states that its MA has been discontinued. The current external directory does not list a Classics MA entry.
conditions: The official current admissions page says discontinued.

facts.value: The application originates with GSB MBA Admissions. Applicants select interest in the joint program in the MBA application and complete an additional essay. Current MBA1 students may apply during their first quarter using the internal joint application. The program is two years full-time.

Apply through the GSE POLS MA application, indicate MA/MPP consideration and complete the joint-degree prompt. If admitted to POLS, GSE forwards the application to Public Policy; POLS admission is required, but MPP admission is separate. Econ 1 and Math 20 are required before matriculation, though not necessarily at application.
conditions: Both programs try to issue concurrent decisions, but timing may differ; final decisions precede April 15.

facts.value: Applicants may apply through the Law School and indicate joint MA/JD interest, or apply after Law School admission before the earlier of the end of JD year two or the GSE deadline for the intended MA start. Both schools must approve the joint course of study.

The History of Art MA is only available to Art & Art History PhD students as progress toward the PhD. The department does not admit students who want only the MA. The PhD field may include Film & Media Studies; doctoral students also complete collateral studies in another graduate department or interdisciplinary program.

Submit three recommendation letters; scanned transcripts for each postsecondary institution attended full-time for at least one academic year; and an SOP of no more than 1,000 words, single spaced, 12-point Times New Roman, 1-inch margins, naming the PhD program and field in its first sentence. One writing sample of at most 20 pages including illustrations and bibliography; full master’s theses are not accepted. GRE is not required. Finalists may be interviewed by faculty via Skype. Autumn-only admission; department page gives December 1, 9 p.m. Pacific deadline and decisions around March 15.
conditions: Department page says TOEFL required when first language is not English and IELTS is not accepted; reconcile with central university policy and exemption criteria.
exceptions: Department deadline page says 9 p.m. Pacific while central Graduate Admissions permits submission by 11:59 p.m. Pacific; verify the stricter department cutoff in live application.

facts.value: Art History PhD normally has a five-year support package from departmental fellowships, teaching and research assistantships; additional support includes summer language study, summer research, and individual research/travel funds. Students select a particular art-history field (including Film & Media Studies), complete collateral graduate study; progress review occurs at end of year two, dissertation topic/proposal by end of year three, and dissertation must be completed within five years after candidacy.
conditions: Support is described as normal rather than a guaranteed award; candidacy completion starts a separate five-year dissertation clock.

facts.value: For 2027-28 GSE coterm entry, Stanford undergraduates need at least 120 units toward graduation, apply to one coterm program per term, and submit the coterm application, preliminary program proposal, statement of purpose, resume, undergraduate transcript and two recommendations. GRE is not required. Deadline January 7, 2027; decisions in early March; accepted applicants respond by April 15, 2027 before completion of their undergraduate degree. The CTE MA accepts no applications for this cycle.

GSE masters programs are largely self-funded. The 2026-27 published cost-of-attendance page gives program-specific budgets for GCE/IEPA, LDT, POLS and EDS; EDS year-two 2027-28 figures are estimates. No one school-wide price applies to STEP or the joint degrees. All domestic and international applicants are automatically considered for Deans Fellowships; the award is included with the admission offer if granted and is final. Zaentz fellowship consideration for EDS, GCE/IEPA, LDT and POLS requires separate early-childhood responses in the online application.

GSE offers all admitted Education PhD students a five-year package of tuition aid, fellowship stipend and assistantship salary covering the standard cost of attendance for the student alone. Assistantship work is part of the package; this is not a funding promise for GSE masters or joint-degree applicants.

Education Data Science MS is a two-year full-time residential program with at least 51 units. It combines coursework in education and data science with an internship and mentored original research projects; its duration and cost cannot be inferred from the one-year MA/MS tracks.

Global and Comparative Education and International Education Policy Analysis are two tracks of a 48-unit MA. Both complete an MA research paper through the EDUC 206 series; GCE and IEPA have distinct track requirements. The program includes summer enrollment.

Learning Design and Technology MS requires at least 45 units, including at least 30 GSE units, over the academic year and summer. It includes internship workshops in at least two quarters, a learning portfolio and a masters design project.

Policy, Organization and Leadership Studies MA requires at least 45 units, including at least 27 GSE units, across Autumn through Spring. Its 2026-27 field placement involves about 150 hours and a project deliverable.

STEP Secondary admits by the intended credential subject: English, history/social science, mathematics, science or world languages. Candidates complete at least 45 units over four quarters, student teaching alongside coursework, an Education MA and a preliminary California single-subject teaching credential.

The Division of Literatures, Cultures, and Languages states all admitted PhD students receive five years of 12-month funding through tuition/fellowship and research or teaching assistantships; its programs do not provide financial support to masters students. Division departments do not grant their own application fee waivers; applicants may review central university waiver routes. The division page currently labels its admission cycle ambiguously, so no deadline is inferred here.

English PhD admits receive five years of 12-month support through fellowship and assistantships, with non-guaranteed sixth-year consideration. PhD candidates demonstrate reading knowledge of one foreign language; the department prefers evidence before admission. Teaching includes a first-year pedagogy seminar and typically three teaching assignments.

Modern Thought and Literature PhD requests a purpose statement no longer than 1,500 words explaining interdisciplinary preparation and a scholarly critical/analytic writing sample of at most 7,000 words; creative writing is not a substitute. No particular undergraduate major is required. Admitted students receive a five-year plan covering tuition and stipend/salary, including five summers.

The Modern Thought and Literature coterm MA is for current Stanford undergraduates well prepared in literature and at least one foreign language, including students from other majors. Its application asks for a roughly 20-page analytical writing sample and is due January 13, 2027.

Religious Studies PhD applicants specify a field, provide an SOP of at most five double-spaced pages, three confidential recommendations, transcripts and a 15-25 page double-spaced English academic writing sample on religion preceded by a short rationale. GRE is optional. Faculty consider prior religious-studies and research-language preparation and fit with faculty resources. Decisions normally arrive late February; offers may be accepted through April 15.

Religious Studies PhD students are eligible for up to five years of funding, including tuition, student Cardinal Care insurance, stipend or teaching assistantships, plus up to five funded summers. The department does not fund coterminal or masters students.

East Asian Studies MA 2027-28 application closes December 3, 2026. External applicants select Humanities/Social Sciences method and China/Japan/Korea region; submit transcripts, three recommendations, purpose statement (recommended at most 1,000 words), and first 15 double-spaced pages of an English academic nonfiction writing sample. GRE is not considered. CEAS offers limited fellowships, contingent on availability; check yes for financial aid in the application. Coterm applicants have different recommendation requirements and are considered for CEAS fellowships only under stated enrollment rules.

Russian, East European and Eurasian Studies MA application deadline is January 12, 2027. External terminal and current Stanford undergraduate coterm applications use separate online routes. External applicants submit transcripts, an at-most-two-page purpose statement, three relevant faculty references (one preferably language instructor), a writing sample of no more than 20 English pages and a list of relevant coursework with grades. Three years of relevant language study is strong preparation, but candidates with less are considered; this is not a hard minimum.

Latin American Studies MA requires Spanish at B1 CEFR/intermediate-high ACTFL or equivalent third-year university study and experience studying, working or living in Latin America/Iberia. External applicants provide a short purpose statement, 150-250 word proposed-research abstract, English academic writing sample and Spanish-fluency statement where their degree was not at a Spanish-language institution. Current Stanford undergraduates may use the coterm route after 120 units. Department fellowships and assistantships are competitive/available rather than guaranteed; applicants indicate aid interest in the online application.

Theater and Performance Studies accepts external PhD applications only, not a terminal MA. It asks for a purpose statement (at most two double-spaced pages), artistic statement (at most three), production-experience summary/CV, one or two scholarly papers totaling no more than 25 pages, transcripts and three recommendations. GRE is not required; a masters is not required. Applicants may be interviewed; decisions are communicated in March. The current official Graduate Admissions directory corroborates the November 24, 2026 deadline in the page header; the body still contains a stale November 25, 2025 date.

Theater and Performance Studies PhD describes a five-year fellowship package with tuition, health insurance, travel award and living stipend. First years emphasize full-time study; later years include teaching and dissertation writing.

Music DMA and PhD doctoral students receive five years of 12-month funding; individual Cardinal Care premiums are covered for three academic quarters in each of the five years. Later assistantships depend on department needs. The Music, Science, and Technology terminal MA does not typically receive department or center funding, although an eligible student may occasionally receive fellowship or teaching support; no award is assured. The department offers no departmental application fee waiver.

Classics PhD offers a six-year funding package conditional on satisfactory progress. Through year five the package provides stipend, tuition and health insurance for four academic quarters per year; it includes five funded summers. Applicants do not file a separate departmental funding application.

The MLA is a part-time, on-campus evening program normally lasting four or five years, with at least 50 units and an interdisciplinary thesis. Most students take one course per quarter. MLA students are not eligible for Stanford graduate housing.

The currently available MLA tuition page quotes $12,708 annual tuition for 2025-26, billed in three installments, with separate document and student-activity fees. This is historical for a 2027 applicant, not a current-cycle quote. Admission is need-blind; the MLA tuition-assistance program seeks to help students with demonstrated need after admission. Part-time MLA students generally lack traditional student-loan eligibility.

For 2027 entry, GSE plans PhD decisions in mid-February and masters/coterm decisions in early March. Responses are due April 15, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific. STEP begins June 21, 2027; other GSE PhD and masters programs begin September 20, 2027. These dates are GSE routes, not joint MBA/JD decisions.

STEP candidates need a bachelors degree before program start. California subject-matter competence may be shown through CSET, qualifying coursework, aligned degree, or approved preparation program; at least half the subject domains are due by program start and all CSET subtests by August. A foreign bachelors degree requires approved equivalency evaluation for California basic-skills credential purposes. The STEP page mixes old cohort dates; verify calendar-specific test deadlines for 2027.

STEP offers need/merit tuition fellowships of $5,000-$35,000 and a small number of full-tuition Stanford Teaching Fellows awards. Qualified future teachers may receive a forgivable loan up to $40,000 tied to teaching at an eligible U.S. school, with half forgiven after two years and the balance after four. Applicants seeking these fellowships complete the STEP supplemental funding section and FAFSA; no award is automatic.

Biology and Biophysics are two of 14 Stanford Biosciences PhD Home Programs spanning Humanities and Sciences and Medicine. They use the shared Biosciences application for Autumn 2027-28, due December 1, 2026 at 11:59:59 p.m. PST. GRE General is not considered for either; Biology does not consider a GRE Subject test, while Biophysics treats Mathematics or Physics Subject scores as optional. The applicant selects a Home Program; these two H&S awards should not be reclassified as School of Medicine awards.

Linguistics accepts only currently enrolled Stanford undergraduates to its coterm MA, not external MA applicants. For Spring 2026-27 entry, application deadline is January 12, 2027. Submit Stanford transcript, purpose statement explaining the MA and possible research paper, adviser-approved program proposal, named Linguistics faculty adviser, and three references including one Linguistics faculty member.
